segments.text: frens.
A friend picks the price where your bitcoin trade should cash out.
You accept it with one tap.
And they only get paid if the price really gets there.
Today that advice lives in a group chat.
Sell at eighty-five thousand.
If it's wrong, it costs the friend nothing.
This is Anna.
She's betting bitcoin goes up, on Perpl, an exchange where you trade on the price of bitcoin.
Her friend Bo thinks bitcoin will climb a bit further before it turns.
He drags a take profit, the price where her trade cashes out, onto her trade, and sends it.
Anna sees Bo's face on the line and taps Accept.
Now her trade will really sell at Beau's price.
Anna puts in two dollars, Beau's reward if he's right.
Bo puts in two dollars to back his pick.
Beau's pick has a deadline.
If bitcoin reaches his price by then, Bo takes all four dollars.
If not, Anna gets all four.
When Bo is right, he gets paid the moment the price gets there.
A second pick, earlier today: Beau picked eighty-five thousand.
It missed, so Anna got all four dollars.
Every friend gets a record: how many of their prices came true, and what they earned.
Anna chooses whose picks she sees.
She adds a friend, removes one, and shares her chart as one link.
A friend picks your price.
You accept with one tap.
They only get paid if the price really gets there.
